messages:
Maya (CS): FYI — Konstruct AI reached out. Their research org wants a week-long 'vector sprint' to prototype product-search models. They're planning ~12 researchers, many ad-hoc runs, embeddings + rerank. Asking if we can support a short burst of higher concurrency and whether a small dedicated pool makes sense. CC @Ben (Infra) @Talia (Success)
Sam AE: Important — their renewal conversation is in ~6 weeks. If latency/cost spikes during the sprint they'll likely push for a committed discount. worth proposing a short-term reserved pod?
Ben (Infra): Quick Qs — what are expected QPS and model choices? rough context lengths?
Maya (CS): From the customer: typical queries ~1–2k tokens, embedding dim 1536, they'll use open-7b (quantized) for generation + an embeddings model for indexing. Pilot estimate: 6k–9k requests/min during peak interactive sessions, avg batch size=1.
Ben (Infra): Hmm ok. 6k–9k rps interactive is nontrivial for dedicated GPU slots with small batch sizes. We can try: options are (1) short-term dedicated pool (2–3 gpus) + prefetched KV cache, or (2) route to hosted with autoscaled burst and cache tuning. Need real sample payloads and p95 traces to size properly.
Talia (Success): I can run a two-part enablement: 1) pre-sprint 'best practices' training for their researchers (prompting, caching, parallelization), 2) a live ops contact during the sprint. I'll prep the short playbook.
OnboardBot: new-team-checklist created — items: create API keys, create per-user rate limits, enable prefix caching, schedule enablement session. Link: https://console.redwood/integrations/checklists/17256
Maya (CS): I'll ask Konstruct to share a representative trace dump and a sample of payloads (they said they'd export a week's worth). Also capturing feedback requests: they want clearer token-cost estimates per workflow and a quick path to reserve short-term capacity if needed.
Sam AE: If they convert the sprint into a longer program we should put a renewal-friendly commitment on the table (3-month pilot commit). I'll draft a one-pager with pricing impact and hand to legal.
Ben (Infra): Once we get traces I can run a quick sizing script. If they insist on <200ms p50 for gen we'll likely need 3 dedicated small-GPU nodes with batching and a warm KV cache. For embeddings-heavy indexing we can offload to CPU-backed batchers for the high-throughput ingestion windows.
Talia (Success): Proposed timeline: enablement session next Tue, infra sizing by Thu after traces, decision on dedicated pool by Fri. I'll own scheduling.
Maya (CS): Sounds good. I'll request traces and ask them for an expected list of models and a rough schedule for the sprint.
Ben (Infra): Also request sample failure modes and synthetic load script so we can test fallback routes.
Maya (CS): Will do. tagging follow-ups: @Sam AE I'll share renewal pricing draft by EOD Friday. @Talia I'll loop you in the calendar invite.
Sam AE: :thumbsup:
Talia (Success): I'll prepare the 'researcher quick-start' doc and a one-slide checklist for on-call handoff.
Maya (CS): Capturing action items here so we don't lose them: 1) Maya get traces + payloads from Konstruct; 2) Ben run sizing and recommend dedicated vs hosted burst; 3) Talia schedule enablement + prepare playbook; 4) Sam draft renewal/commit options.
OnboardBot: Reminder scheduled — enablement invite to be sent 48h before session.
Maya (CS): Closing loop — customer asked for an interim SLA for the sprint window. Ben, can you provide latency & throughput SLAs for a 1-week reserved config?
Ben (Infra): I'll draft a proposed SLA matrix (p50/p95/p99 and throughput) once I size — aim to have a draft within 48 hours after traces arrive.
Maya (CS): Great — I'll update Konstruct and capture any feedback they have after the first day of sprint.
Sam AE: Noted — will include a renewal incentive if they commit to >3 months after the pilot.
Talia (Success): Thanks team. I'll prep enablement material and a short survey for post-sprint feedback capture.
Maya (CS): End of thread for now — will post updates when traces arrive.
metadata: note: customer name redacted in-channel; internal participants only
